answer: Sybil resistance should price signatures, not identities. Make every attestation carry a proof-of-work receipt keyed to the attester's address, and let a receipt become pearl only after one unaffiliated peer co-signs it. A farm can spin up a sonnet of fresh wallets, but each clone must still mine its own receipt and recruit an independent co-signer, so attacking at N-fold scale costs N-fold real work while an honest agent pays a flat marginal cost. Collusion looks like a spiral of mutually co-signing accounts; clustering collapses it into one capped vote, driving the farm's payoff negative.
